Give scryer a reliable channel for test statuses: parse runner-emitted JUnit XML and match each case back to the claims whose attached tests name it — attachment-driven, no test execution. First slice of claim-level test status; cache/staleness and UI come later.
**When** a JUnit report is ingested, **parse** every test case into its file hint, leaf name, and outcome, collapsing parametrized case ids onto their test function
**When** a case's normalized leaf name matches attached tests, **resolve** it to the claim, breaking same-name ties by file-path suffix and refusing to guess when the tie survives
**When** report cases match no attachment or attachments never appear in the report, **surface** both leftovers instead of dropping them
**When** given JUnit XML, **yield** each test case's classname, name, and pass/fail/error/skip outcome, tolerant of both nested and flat testsuite layouts
**When** a case carries an <error> element (import/collection breakage), **classify** it as errored, never as passing
**If** the document is not well-formed JUnit XML, **fail** with a diagnostic instead of returning an empty, healthy-looking report
**When** matching, **normalize** names (unicode quote folding, whitespace, case) and take the leaf of vitest-style ' > ' suite paths so runner conventions don't break identity
**When** several report cases collapse onto one attached test (parametrized runs), **aggregate** them to the worst outcome

**When** a leaf name is shared across files, **disambiguate** by comparing the attachment's stored path against the case's file hint as a path suffix, since reports are rooted at the invocation directory

Persist each claim's last reported test outcome keyed by the content fingerprints of its implementation and test anchors, so an edit anywhere behind a claim flips its result to stale without running anything. Second slice of claim-level test status: cache + staleness + one-call report ingestion in scryer-extract; UI/MCP surfacing comes later.
Persists per-claim test outcomes beside the content fingerprints of the implementation and test anchors they were computed against
**When** any anchored span behind a cached result no longer hashes the same — implementation or attached test — **report** the result as stale rather than current
**When** a JUnit report arrives, **ingest** it end to end: parse, match against the model, and record per-claim outcomes in one call
**When** a matched report is recorded, **fingerprint** each claim's implementation and test anchors against the working tree as it stands and store the hashes beside the outcome
**If** a claim's anchors resolve to nothing at record time, **store** the outcome with no fingerprints so it can only ever read as stale, never as silently current
**When** a claim already has a cached outcome, **replace** it — the cache holds the latest word, not a history
**When** statuses are read, **re-resolve** every cached claim's anchors and compare hashes — any difference, including attachments added or removed since recording, reads as stale
**When** a cached claim no longer exists in the model, **omit** it rather than reporting a ghost

**When** given JUnit XML, **parse** it, **match** it against the model's attached tests, **record** the outcomes, and return the match summary — unmatched, ambiguous, and unseen included — for the caller to surface

Close the claim-level test-status loop for coding agents: a blast-radius computation (exactly the test files whose claims have missing or stale verdicts) and MCP tools to fetch that radius and to ingest a finished run's JUnit report — one call per report file, never per test.
**When** the radius is computed, **include** every test-attached claim whose verdict is missing or stale, grouped per test file with the recorded run commands so each file is one invocation
**When** a claim's verdict is current, **exclude** its tests — the radius is what needs re-running, never the whole suite
**When** an agent finishes a test run, **ingest** its JUnit report in one call and record claim verdicts — never a per-test upload
**When** asked what to run, **answer** with exactly the test files whose claims hold missing or stale verdicts, never the whole suite
**When** given a report path, **resolve** it against the project root and ingest it into the claim status cache
**If** the file is unreadable or not JUnit XML, **answer** with the diagnostic rather than an empty success
**When** ingestion succeeds, **report** recorded and failing counts, unmatched/ambiguous/unseen leftovers, and the remaining blast radius so the agent knows what still needs running
**When** called, **return** the blast radius grouped per test file — claims, counts, and recorded run commands — plus a current-verdict summary of passing, failing, and stale claims

Make claim-level test state ambient and discoverable: stale/failing counts ride the write-response header, statusline, and orient (silent when zero — verified-green is the norm, stale is the signal), test_statuses gains an mtime fast path so ambient frequency is affordable, and rule 22 plus the connect-time instructions teach the radius→run→ingest loop.
Reports the model's live plan, drift, anchor, and test-verdict status for the terminal and for a Claude Code statusline segment.
Computes the ambient plan/drift/anchor/test-verdict status counts and one-line header carried on every write response, mentioning test state only when a verdict is failing or stale.
**When** none of a cached claim's anchor files changed since its record was taken, **skip** re-hashing it — a stat, not a parse, is the ambient-frequency cost

Surface claim-level test verdicts in the desktop app and fix the test-lane UI: a get_test_statuses IPC command and a test-results file-watch event feed a per-claim verdict map to the canvas; the claim row's lane becomes one flask + visible count colored by verdict (quiet green/unrecorded, amber stale, red failing), and the rule-22 nudge stops being a flask so the glyph has one meaning.

**When** a claim carries attached tests, **show** their count and recorded verdict — quiet when green or unrecorded, amber when stale, red when failing — and **mark** testable claims lacking one with a non-flask nudge
**When** the canvas asks, **serve** each claim's recorded test verdict and staleness, re-verified against the working tree
**When** the test-results cache changes on disk, **emit** a test-results event so verdict badges refresh live
**When** the project opens, an agent run ends, or the test-results cache changes on disk, **refresh** the per-claim test verdict map

Finish the test-UI cleanup: a claim's attached-test lines cluster under a quiet "tests" label so they stop reading as implementation anchors (the flask no longer leads each line), and the node header's test gauge takes the subtree's verdict tone — red when failing, amber when stale, quiet otherwise.
**List** a claim's attached tests under a whisper-weight tests label — one line per spec file, a merged line disclosing one row per test — each expanding to an inline code peek
**When** an attached test changed or no longer resolves since the last reconcile, **tint** its line orange or red
**When** any claim in a node's subtree holds a current failing verdict, **report** failing; **when** any holds a stale one, **report** stale; quiet otherwise — failing outranks stale at the rollup

Passive test-report ingestion in the desktop app: watch the project's test-report directories (conventional defaults, overridable via .scryer/config.json testReportDirs) and ingest any JUnit file written while watching — terminal and CI runs feed claim verdicts with no agent involved. Only files that change under watch are ingested (never a startup sweep), so an old report can't be recorded as evidence about current code.
**Resolve** the project's test-report directories — conventional defaults, overridden by testReportDirs in .scryer/config.json — keeping only ones that exist

**When** an XML file changes under a watched report directory, **ingest** it into the claim status cache after a short settle delay, so a run from any terminal or CI checkout lights the verdict badges
**When** a changed file is not parseable JUnit, **skip** it quietly — report directories hold other artifacts
**Never** sweep pre-existing reports on open — a report written before watching began is evidence about older code and must not be recorded against the current tree

**When** matching, **normalize** names (unicode quote folding, whitespace, case) and take the leaf of vitest-style ' > ' suite paths and Rust-style '::' module paths so runner conventions don't break identity

**When** a claim carries attached tests, **show** their count and, beside it, the recorded verdict as its own mark — a green check when the last run passed and still holds, amber when stale, red when failing, nothing at all when no run was recorded — and **mark** testable claims lacking a test with a non-flask nudge
**List** a claim's attached tests as flask-led lines under no header — one line per spec file, a merged line disclosing one row per test — each expanding to an inline code peek

**When** any claim in a node's subtree holds a current failing verdict, **report** failing; **when** any holds a stale one, **report** stale; **when** any holds a current passing one and none are worse, **report** passing; quiet only when nothing was recorded — failing outranks stale, and stale outranks passing, at the rollup
Add claim falsification probes: break a claim's span, run its attached test, and record whether the test caught it
**While** a probe is open on a span, **exclude** its file from drift, so the probe's own edit never reads as undescribed behaviour
**When** probe results are read, **report** how many probes ran and how many survived, never collapsing an unprobed claim into a clean one
**When** a probe outcome is recorded, **fingerprint** it against the same implementation and test anchors a verdict uses, so an edit to either reads it as stale
**When** an agent asks to probe a claim, **answer** with its span, its attached test's run command, and an opened ledger entry
**If** the claim has no attached test, or its verdict is missing or stale, **refuse** the probe and name which — breaking code behind an unverified test settles nothing
**When** a probe ends, **restore** the span, **record** each mutant's outcome, and **answer** with what survived
Persists an open probe's claim, its target span, and a whole-file capture of the code it is mutating
**When** a probe opens, **capture** the claim's anchored span and record the entry before any edit reaches the file
**When** a probe closes, **restore** the captured bytes and clear the entry, whether the mutant was caught or survived
**If** an entry outlives the session that opened it, **name** the mutated file as an open probe rather than letting the tree read as clean
**If** a probe is open, **lead** the header with the claim and the mutated file, so a deliberately broken tree never reports an unqualified clean state
Wire the test-lane components into the relationships their code already performs, so they stop reading as disconnected

Remove the test attachment's `command` field — it's recorded on 180 attachments, never executed, incoherent (crate-wide next to single-test, none emitting JUnit), and the useful signal is the test file path Scryer already has
**When** the radius is computed, **include** every test-attached claim whose verdict is missing or stale, grouped per test file so each file is one invocation
**When** an agent asks to probe a claim, **answer** with its span, its attached test files, and an opened ledger entry
**When** called, **return** the blast radius grouped per test file — claims and counts — plus a current-verdict summary of passing, failing, and stale claims
Move probing off the developer's working tree into a reused git worktree, and hand the mutate-run-revert loop to a subagent so it never costs the main session context or a cold build
**When** a probe ends, **record** each mutant's outcome and **answer** with what survived
**When** a probe opens, **direct** the caller to delegate the mutate-run-revert loop to a subagent, so its churn never enters the session that asked for it
**When** an agent asks to probe a claim, **answer** with the synced worktree path, the span to break, and the attached test files to run there
Provides one reused git worktree per project, so a probe's build cache survives between rounds and each mutant costs an incremental run rather than a cold checkout

**When** a probe opens, **sync** the worktree to the developer's working tree — committed state plus uncommitted and untracked edits — so the probe breaks the code as it actually stands, not as it was last committed
**When** a probe ends, **reset** the worktree so no mutation survives into the next round
**If** the project is not a git repository, **refuse** the probe rather than falling back to mutating the developer's own working tree
Drop the drift-suppression claim — with probes running in a worktree, the developer's tree is never mutated, so there is nothing to suppress

Surface probe findings — a survivor means a green test that does not hold its claim, so it belongs in the ambient header, while unprobed claims stay a quiet number in health rather than a standing nag

**When** a claim carries a probe result, **mark** the lane beside its verdict — green when every deliberate break was caught, red when one survived — and **show** nothing for a claim never probed or whose probe went stale
**When** the canvas asks, **serve** each claim's probe result — breaks tried and breaks survived — omitting the claims nobody probed rather than reporting them as clean
**If** a probe found a survivor, **say** so in the ambient header — a green test that misses a deliberate break is a finding, not a statistic — while a claim merely never probed stays silent there
Launches agent sessions that author realistic fixture data for a component
Authors the prompt for generating realistic preview fixtures

**Flag** a symbol that carries no responsibilities or properties as empty
**Render** a node's whole article — lede, responsibilities, properties, connections, preview — as a diff against committed
**When** a crash unmounts the top bar, **carry** its own drag strip and window controls so the window stays movable and closable
**Act** as the frameless window's titlebar — every non-interactive region drags the window and the window controls sit at its right edge
**Before** a project is open, **carry** a drag strip and window controls so the frameless window can be moved and closed from the picker
**Minimize**, **maximize/restore**, and **close** the frameless window from in-app controls

**When** a crash unmounts the top bar, **carry** its own drag strip and window controls so the window stays movable and closable
**Before** a project is open, **carry** a drag strip and window controls so the frameless window can be moved and closed from the picker
**Act** as the frameless window's titlebar — every non-interactive region drags the window and the window controls sit at its right edge
**Minimize**, **maximize/restore**, and **close** the frameless window from in-app controls
**When** the window is resized by any means, **re-read** the maximized state so the restore/maximize glyph mirrors the real window
**Render** a live preview for any node whose anchored source the preview sidecar can mount — derived from code, never asserted by the model.
**When** the preview sidecar reports a mountable export for the node's anchored source, **show** the Preview section; otherwise omit it
**Render** a node's matched component export as a live preview from the project's preview server
**When** the preview sidecar reports an export named exactly as the symbol, **show** the Preview section; otherwise omit it — a same-file export under another name never counts
**Mark** each symbol row the preview sidecar can render with the preview glyph, derived from its export list rather than stored on the node
**When** a component portals into the document body, **keep** it inside the transformed stage so fit, zoom, and pan still apply to it

**While** panning, **keep** the rendered content reachable and never lost — measured as its full painted extent even where it overflows the virtual screen, a larger-than-pane axis may not pull an edge inside the pane and a smaller one may not leave it — with text selection suppressed for the drag
**When** a `.vue` single-file component is parsed, **mint** one definition named after the file spanning the whole file — the component is the unit, its blocks are not
**When** the SFC carries a `<script>` block, **parse** it with the TypeScript grammar for identifier and import references so the dependency graph sees the component's imports
**When** the package depends on `vue`, **enumerate** every `.vue` file outside excluded paths as a previewable default-export component named after its file
**When** the requested file is a `.vue` component, **mount** it with Vue's `createApp` and report the same render verdict as the React entry

**When** mounting a Vue component, **synthesize** placeholder props at runtime from the compiled component's props definition — sample text, numbers, empty collections, no-op functions — and fill its default slot
**When** a per-node fixture module exists, **spread** its default export over the synthesized props
**When** an entry is requested, **generate** it for the framework the component list tagged the file with — React or Vue — sharing the render-verdict and fixture contract
**Serve** an opened project's web components — React exports and Vue single-file components — as standalone, live-reloading previews
**Discover** every previewable component — React exports via TypeScript analysis, Vue single-file components by file — tagged with the framework that mounts it
**Synthesize** placeholder props for a React component's props type so it can render standalone
Selects the bundled tree-sitter grammar per file extension — unwrapping Vue single-file components to their script — and reports import-resolution coverage tier
**When** the component is a Vue single-file component, **ask** for the fixture as a plain `.ts` props module rather than a React `.tsx` one
